cohort: The study included peripartum UK obstetric admissions from 192 consultant-led obstetric units within UK National Health Service (NHS) hospitals.
finding: The estimated incidence of symptomatic peripartum hyponatraemia was 3.0 cases per 100,000 maternities and was associated with maternal morbidity, high neonatal morbidity, and a high rate of operative birth.
mod_finding: Operative birth was high in cases of peripartum hyponatraemia, even without documented maternal symptoms, while 38% of cases with documented symptoms and 20% without symptoms had a spontaneous vaginal birth.
